composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-110a, "24V DC SERVICE SUPPLY") is the PORT/STBD HVPDU → MAPS → 24V DC service-bus one-line: it shows the 600V DC HVPDU buses (both sides) feeding MAPS-1/2 converters that step down to 24V DC, monitored via CT1-CT5 to ONYX, then routed through an isolator/contactor (SW/SO) bank onto the +24V SERVICE BUS which fuses out to FWD/AFT DC panels, BILGE PUMP, FIRE PUMP, AUX SERVICE BAT., and (via SW11/F16) toward GEN START BAT charging. A separate 230VAC/24VDC 110A supply plus Re1/Re2 relay logic drives BAE START KEY SW / Service Mode signalling into a PC CARD that also carries BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL indicators. The sheet therefore serves: 620-hvpdu (both HVPDU buses + Q1-Q4/F1-F2 breakers, established fact), 626-maps-p / 626-maps-s (the two MAPS-1/2 converter pairs), 640-dc-distribution (the +24V service bus, FWD/AFT DC panel taps), 520-main-bilge-pump and 520-fire-pump (named load taps off the bus), 634-battery-aux-service (AUX SERVICE BAT 200Ah 24V with SW11/F16 — matches established F16 fact), 633-battery-gen-start (to GEN START BAT tap), 652-onyx-monitoring (all CT1-CT6 taps 'to ONYX'), 625-bae-system (BAE START KEY SW / Service Mode / BAE VOLTAGE SENCE cross-ref to DWG 413), and 629-bel1-p (BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL, cross-ref DWG 401a, consistent with established BEL-1 PORT node).

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet shows both PORT and STBD 600V DC HVPDU buses with Q1-Q4 32A breakers and F1/F2 500A fuses, matching the established HVPDU identity fact (Q1-4 32A breakers, F1/F2 500A fuses per side). These buses ARE the HVPDU per established fact — not a separate backbone.

functions.what_it_does: Distributes 600V DC from each HVPDU bus through four 32A breakers (Q1-Q4) into the respective PORT/STBD MAPS-1/2 converters, protected upstream by F1/F2 500A fuses per side.

flow_scenarios.path: PORT/STBD 600V DC bus -> Q1-Q4 32A breakers -> feed to MAPS-1/2 2x5KW converter inputs (600V DC side)

equipment_groups.equipment_name: BAE Hybrid System (hub) — start-key / service-mode signalling
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The 24V 110A/230VAC power supply feeds a relay/terminal-strip logic block (Re1/Re2, T/S S) explicitly labeled 'BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode)' with a cross-reference 'to Re 2a (see DWG 113)' and 'BAE VOLTAGE SENCE (see DWG 413)' — this is BAE hybrid system control signalling, not the DC distribution panel itself.

functions.label: BAE start-key / service-mode signal generation
functions.what_it_does: A dedicated 24V 110A AC/DC supply (230VAC in, 24VDC/125A fused out via F18) powers a relay bank (Re1, Re2) switched via terminal strip contacts (T/S S terminals 1-7 and 5-12), producing the BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode) signal and continuing off-sheet to Re2a (DWG 113).

flow_scenarios.path: 230V AC (L/N) -> 24V 110A supply -> fuse F18 125A -> 24V DC out -> switches 1-4 on T/S S terminals 1-4/4-7 -> relay bank (Re1 top, Re2 lower, plus two more relay positions) -> BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode) output -> onward to Re 2a (see DWG 113)
T/S S terminal group (terminals 5-12) -> BAE VOLTAGE SENCE tap -> see DWG 413
